transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve just been forgetting little things more than I should. Like calls I’m supposed to return, or a registration form I needed to turn in, or an errand I meant to stop for on the way home. It’s not huge stuff, but it’s been happening enough that I thought I should ask about it.
When you forget these things, does it usually happen because your mind was somewhere else and you weren’t fully paying attention at the time?

Yeah… I think so. Like at work, if a phone rings or people are talking nearby, I can get pulled off whatever I was doing. Sometimes it’s just a thought about something at home, and then I lose track a bit.
Looking back to when you were a child, did you also have a hard time staying focused?

Yeah… I think so. I wasn’t really a troublemaker or anything, but I’d forget permission slips, or lose homework in my backpack. For bigger projects, my mom or the teacher usually had to remind me what to do next, step by step.
Do these focus and forgetfulness problems cause significant trouble for you at work?

A little, yeah. I’m still getting by at work, but I’ve missed some small follow-ups and deadlines often enough that I worry people notice. I’m hoping to move into an Office Manager role eventually, and… I don’t want this to hurt my chances.
Do you often find yourself worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?
Um… I don’t know. I worry about stuff sometimes, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say it’s all the time or about everything. Not that I’ve really noticed.
Do you notice these focus and forgetfulness problems outside of work too?

Yeah… it happens at home too. Mostly little things I’m supposed to handle, like returning a call, turning in some form, or remembering to stop for an errand on the way home. It’s kind of what finally made me think I should ask someone about it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Not really… I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed.
Before age 12, were you already having these kinds of attention or forgetfulness problems?

Yeah… I think so. In elementary school I was kind of that kid who’d forget permission slips, or lose homework somewhere in my backpack. My mom or my teacher usually had to walk me through projects step by step or I just wouldn’t finish them.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or activities?

Yeah… somewhat. I can usually keep up at work, but since I started evening classes, things get messy fast. My desk, my class folder, email reminders… they all kind of turn into piles, and then I waste time just figuring out what I’m supposed to do first.
Did these focus and forgetfulness problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful life change?
Yeah… I think it got harder when I started my evening certificate classes. That was about… 15 months ago. It’s not like it started then, but it’s been more noticeable since then.
Have you noticed your memory getting worse compared with a few years ago?

Maybe a little, yeah. I’m not sure if it’s “memory” exactly, but lately I keep forgetting small things I usually manage… like returning calls, turning in a registration form, or stopping for an errand on the way home. That’s kind of what made me ask for help.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, maybe I blank on a word once in a while, but nothing that’s stood out to me.
Have these problems led you to need more help than usual with everyday tasks you used to manage on your own?

A little, yeah. I’m still mostly managing on my own, but I’ve had to lean on reminders and sometimes people checking in more than I used to. I’ve missed small follow-ups at work and a few school deadlines, and… I worry it makes me look unreliable, especially if I want to move into an Office Manager role.
Compared with earlier in your adult life, do these attention and forgetting problems feel clearly worse now?

Yeah… I’d say they’re more noticeable now. It’s been harder to keep on top of things since I started the evening certificate program, about… 15 months ago. Before that I had some issues, but it didn’t feel quite as hard to manage.
Has anyone close to you told you that your memory or thinking seems worse than it used to be?
Not really… no one’s said it like that to me. Maybe people remind me about things, but I don’t think anyone’s told me my memory or thinking seems worse.
Do you ever need help managing your bills or finances because of these problems?

Not really bills, no. It’s more… little things I normally handle, like returning calls or turning in a form, or remembering to stop for an errand on the way home. That’s kind of what made me ask for help.
Have you had any formal testing that showed your attention or memory is worse than it used to be?
No… I haven’t had any formal testing like that. Not that I know of.
Has a doctor, teacher, or employer ever documented that your attention or memory got worse compared with before?
No… not that I’m aware of. I don’t think anyone’s written anything like that down.
Has anyone who knows you well noticed that your thinking or memory has clearly gotten worse over time?
Not really. I mean… no one’s told me that my thinking or memory has clearly gotten worse over time.
Do these attention problems show up in more than one part of your life?

Yeah… it’s not just one place. I’m still getting by, but it happens at work and with school stuff too. I’ll miss little follow-ups or deadlines, and… it worries me a bit, like it could make people think I’m not ready for an Office Manager position.

final_diagnosis.reason: The history is most consistent with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation: longstanding inattentive symptoms beginning in childhood, present across multiple settings, with current functional impact at work, home, and school. Reported worsening after added academic demands reflects increased visibility of chronic attentional deficits rather than a new neurocognitive disorder.
